Wesa warriors.|Jar Jar Binks|}} '''Gungans''' were an [[Amphibian|amphibious]] [[Sentience|sentient]] [[species]] and the indigenous inhabitants of the [[planet]] [[Naboo]]. The various different Gungan races could live on both [[water]] and land, but often made their home in underwater [[City|cities]] such as [[Otoh Gunga]]. Physically, Gungans were tall [[humanoid]]s with a flexible structure, strong leg muscles, strong bills, muscular tongues, and many other traits designed for living in the waters of Naboo. They had strong accents when speaking in [[Galactic Basic Standard]]. Gungans were also known to rarely leave Naboo. The Gungans had a tense and uneasy relationship with the non-native [[human]] [[Naboo (people)|Naboo people]] until the [[Trade Federation]] [[Invasion of Naboo|invasion]]. As a result of the invasion, the Gungans joined forces with the Naboo to [[Battle of Naboo|expel]] the Trade Federation from their homeworld. Following the invasion, [[Jar Jar Binks]] would become the [[Junior Representative]] of the Gungan people in the [[Galactic Senate]], serving alongside [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] of the Naboo. ==Biology and appearance== {{Quote|Jar Jar sealed my helmet with his…''"
"''Yesa! Isa Gungan waterproofing! Isa why wesa swim so good!|Padmé Amidala and Jar Jar Binks, after the latter sealed the former's helmet with his spit|{{TCW|Prisoners}}}} [[File:PeppiBowFull-TCWCEJtB.png|thumb|left|200px|Peppi Bow, a female Otolla Gungan shaak herder]] The Gungans were a [[Sentience|sentient]] [[Amphibian|amphibious]] [[species]]. They were tall humanoids with a flexible structure and strong leg muscles which allowed them to live in the waters of [[Naboo]].{{SWE|groups|gungans|Gungans}} Although Gungans' lives revolved around water, they did not need it to thrive and could settle far from it.''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' Indeed, they could move between land and water without difficulty.{{InsiderCite|221|A Certain Point of View}} Although their native water was the fresh waters of Naboo, they were able to survive in salt water, such as the [[Ocean|sea]]s of [[Mon Cala]].[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Four]] Born as tadpoles, Gungan infants developed limbs within months of being hatched. Accordingly, younglings would have to learn how to walk at an early age, after they learned how to swim with legs.{{GalacticPals|Gungan}} Equipped with hardy [[lung]]s, they were capable of holding their breath for extended periods of time. Their body produced a mucus with waterproofing properties that assisted them when moving through water and they were capable of spitting it over a distance with great force, even when underwater. Their [[Skeleton|skeletal]] structure was extremely flexible, as it was made of cartilaginous material rather than hard [[bone]]. The long Gungan face had a tough yet flexible bill for burrowing and rooting out food. Some Gungans, such as [[Roos Tarpals]], had whiskers on their bills. These whiskers were signs of maturity among Gungans.''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' They had long muscular tongues with which they could scoop mollusks and lesser amphibians from the Naboo swamps, which they were comfortable eating raw. There were two Gungan [[Subspecies|races]]: the lanky [[Otolla]], who sported prominent bills and [[eye]]s set on short stalks, and the heavier [[Ankura]], whose eyes were hooded. The Gungan earlobes called [[haillu]], were most prominent in the Otolla. ==History== [[File:FrontLines-Gunganvictory.png|thumb|right|300px|Gungans played a large role in the Battle of Naboo]] The Gungan species originated on the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] [[Planet|world]] of Naboo, which they shared with a [[human]] civilization known as the [[Naboo (people)|Naboo]] that grew out of the [[Grizmallti]] colonists. The [[human-Gungan conflicts]] were waged between the human colonists and the Gungans. Later, a [[Gungan tribal war]] was waged that ultimately united the assorted Gungan tribes under the banner of Boss [[Gallo]]. During the [[High Republic Era]], a Gungan [[scientist]] named [[Thaddeus Wolk]] was considered a leader in the field of [[theoretical hyperspace physics]] and taught [[Chancey Yarrow]] at the [[Carida Academy|Academy of Carida]] until she got kicked out for theorizing about the creation of an artificial [[gravity well projector]] which she eventually designed for use by the [[Nihil]]. Determined to stop Yarrow from creating the gravity well projector, Wolk was [[assassin]]ated on [[Coruscant]] before he could try to stop her.''[[The High Republic: Out of the Shadows]]'' In [[228 BBY]],''[[The High Republic: Temptation of the Force]]'' establishes that [[Naboo]] became part of the [[Occlusion Zone]] following the [[Expansion of the Stormwall|Stormwall's first expansion]] but before the events of the novel. [[The High Republic Adventures (2023) 4|''The High Republic Adventures'' (2023) 4]] and ''Temptation of the Force'' commence one [[Standard year|year]] and two [[Standard week|weeks]] and one year and six weeks after the [[Destruction of Starlight Beacon|Starlight Beacon's destruction]], respectively, dating both to [[228 BBY]] per the reasoning [[:Template:StarlightDate|here]]. As [[The High Republic Adventures (2023) 6|''The High Republic Adventures'' (2023) 6]]—which depicts the Stormwall's first expansion—takes place immediately following ''The High Republic Adventures'' (2023) 4, Naboo must have been brought into the Occlusion Zone in 228 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. As ''Temptation of the Force'' establishes that Naboo was conquered after it was brought into the Occlusion Zone, it must have occurred that year. the [[Nihil]] expanded their [[Stormwall]] to cut off Naboo from the [[Galactic Republic]]. While the Nihil [[Occupation of Naboo|occupied]] the planet, the Gungans retreated to their underwater cities and went into hiding.''[[Temptation of the Force]]'' In [[32 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' relations between the Gungans and the Naboo were still tense but had not involved an [[Gungan-Naboo dispute|active dispute]] for generations.''[[Queen's Peril]]'' The [[Trade Federation]] [[Invasion of Naboo|invasion]] of Naboo would prove to finally alter Gungan-Naboo relations. One Gungan exile named [[Jar Jar Binks]] befriended the Naboo [[Monarch of Naboo|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] and convinced her to seek the help of the Gungans. Amidala succeeded in [[Boss Meetup|winning over]] the Gungan ruler [[Boss]] [[Rugor Nass|Nass]] and the two peoples formed an alliance to drive out the Trade Federation. During the [[Battle of Naboo]], the [[Gungan Grand Army]] confronted the Federation's [[droid]] army outside [[Theed]], which enabled Amidala's forces to seize back the [[capital]] and capture the Trade Federation's [[Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]]. After the invasion established positive relations between the Gungans and the Naboo, the Gungans were given the right to cast votes in the planet's elections.''[[Queen's Shadow]]'' During the [[Separatist Crisis]], Jar Jar Binks served as the [[Junior Representative]] of the Gungan people in the [[Galactic Senate]]. He played an important role in supporting legislation which led to the creation of a [[Grand Army of the Republic]].{{Film|II}} The Gungans remained loyal to the [[Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. Gungan forces took part in the [[Battle of Mon Cala]] and assisted Prince [[Lee-Char]]'s [[Mon Calamari]] forces and Republic allies against [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] [[Confederacy military|forces]] and their [[Quarren]] allies. [[File:RishLooManipulatingBossLyonie.png|thumb|left|250px|Rish Loo and Boss Lyonie during the Clone Wars]] As the Clone Wars escalated, growing tensions between the Gungans and the Naboo were fueled by rumors that the Gungans were planning to aid a Separatist invasion of Naboo. Under the influence of his pro-Separatist adviser [[Rish Loo]], the reigning Boss [[Lyonie]] ordered the Gungan Grand Army to march on Theed in a coordinated strike with a [[Separatist Droid Army]] led by [[General]] [[Grievous]]. However, Binks, with the help of [[Senator]] Amidala and [[Anakin Skywalker]], succeeded in exposing Rish Loo's conspiracy. Unfortunately, Rish Loo wounded Lyonie before he could call off the attack. Binks then impersonated Lyonie and ordered the Grand Army to abort their assault on Theed. Gungan forces led by Roos Tarpals also played a role in [[Skirmish on Naboo|capturing]] Grievous but were forced to release him after [[Count]] [[Dooku]] threatened to [[Death|kill]] Skywalker.{{TCW|Shadow Warrior}} Following the [[Battle of Endor]], the Gungans confirmed the presence of typhoon-strength storms all over Naboo. These storms were created by several [[climate disruption array]] [[satellite]]s deployed by the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Torment]]'' as part of [[Operation: Cinder]], a secret Imperial plan to scour Naboo and several worlds. Before the Imperials could render Naboo uninhabitable, a [[New Republic]] [[New Republic Defense Fleet|fleet]] arrived and [[Battle of Theed|destroyed]] the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Imperial Military|forces]]; saving the planet.[[Shattered Empire 3|''Shattered Empire'' 3]] In [[9 ABY]],{{MandoDate|6}} during a [[Bothan-Five incident|mission]] to rescue the [[Twi'lek]] [[Qin]] from a [[New Republic Correctional Transport]], the criminal [[Migs Mayfeld]] mocked his associate [[Din Djarin]], a [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] and follower of the [[Way of the Mandalore]] who was not allowed to remove his [[helmet]]. Using an affectation in his voice, Mayfeld sarcastically guessed that Djarin was actually an embarrassed Gungan who refused to show his face.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 6: The Prisoner}} While traveling on an [[automated sidewalk]] in the [[New Republic senatorial complex]] on [[Hosnian Prime]], Senator [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] spotted a Gungan having an animated conversation via his [[comlink]].[[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']] ==Society and culture== [[File:Gungan_High_Council.png|thumb|right|250px|The Gungan government was led by the High Council]] The Gungan government comprised city-based clans and city governments that answered to a [[Gungan High Council|High Council]], which dealt with disputes between cities. Highly stratified, the society placed a high value on overall peace, shunned violence, and condemned even minor crimes such as vandalism with corporal punishments or exile. Each city maintained an army to defend its honor and bolster its pride in its own territories and dominions. Though sometimes dismissed as primitive, the Gungans had advanced technology, including bubble projectors, [[Tribubble bongo|bongo submarines]] and weaponry. The Gungans preferred using technology that was related in some way to the ecology of their world. For example, they used energy [[plasma]] that was mined from their planet's crust to power their cities and their weapons. The Gungans also domesticated animals for use in transport and combat, such as the [[kaadu]], the [[falumpaset]] and the [[fambaa]]. Taming with a kaadu, bonding with the animal in the process, was a sign of reaching adulthood in Gungan culture. Fambaas were also a vital part of Gungan culture because they, like the Gungans, could move from land to water easily. [[File:Gungans.png|thumb|left|225px|The Gungan Grand Army]] Unlike their human neighbors, the Gungans were a proud warrior race, and maintained a large Gungan Grand Army, which acted as the standing Gungan defense force.{{SWE|groups|gungangrandarmy|Gungan Grand Army}} It participated in the Battle of Naboo during the Trade Federation's occupation of the planet. During the Clone Wars, the Grand Army saw action against Separatist forces on both [[Mon Cala]] and later Naboo itself. By the time of the [[Invasions of Naboo]], the inhabitants of [[Otoh Gunga]] were reputed to produce a dessert that took at least four hominids to consume. This dessert was said to be capable of delivering one into a sugar coma.''[[Lost Stars]]'' The rate of [[Force-sensitive]]s in the Gungan society was low, and no native traditions ever emerged. Few Gungans ever joined the [[Jedi Order]], and none were ever reported as becoming [[Sith]], contrary to the rumor that Jar Jar Binks was [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], though at least one Gungan, [[Roo-Roo Page]] was found to be [[Force-sensitive]] and was thus, a target of [[Darth Sidious]] for her Force potential.''[[The Legends of Luke Skywalker]]''{{TCW|Children of the Force}} Culturally, the Gungans were in tune with the [[Living Force]] and had a working understanding of it. ==Gungans in the galaxy== Gungans rarely left Naboo, preferring to remain on their homeworld and help its ecosystems thrive. The only Gungans seen abroad tended to be exiles, cast out from their society on Naboo by the strict, unforgiving laws that governed their people. [[File:JarJarDestroysTheRepublic-AotC.jpg|thumb|right|225px|Jar Jar Binks, Gungan Representative in the Galactic Senate]] One notable Gungan was Jar Jar Binks, a former outcast who brought his people and the Naboo together and later became a Junior Representative in the Galactic Senate. Later, Binks was ostracized by many adult Gungans and Naboo due to his role in aiding the rise of the Empire. Binks later found work as a professional [[clown]] entertaining displaced refugee children. Other noteworthy Gungans included the scientist Thaddeus Wolk, the warrior Roos Tarpals, Otoh Gunga's ruler Boss Nass and his successor Lyonie, the [[shaak]] herder [[Peppi Bow]], and the minister Rish Loo. [[File:Gungan skull.jpg|left|thumb|225x225px|An ancient Gungan skull]] A Gungan [[Bone|skull]] adorned with mysterious symbols and inlaid [[aurodium]] was acquired by the collector [[Luthen Rael]] and displayed at his shop [[Galactic Antiquities and Objects of Interest]] on [[Coruscant]] in [[1 BBY]].{{SW|url=news/andor-luthens-gallery-easter-eggs|text=''Andor'': Even More Hidden Treasures in Luthen Rael's Gallery - Update}} ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|There was some pretty big effort by us and George ''[Lucas]'' to say that, outside of Jar Jar, the Gungans themselves aren't a goofy group. They're not all tripping over their spears and awkwardly running around. Jar Jar's kind of the anomaly there. They're actually quite efficient warriors. You know, large, amphibious creatures would be pretty daunting to anyone. Though, I think that made them viable as a combatant, even though Jar Jar often times is at the front of the group.|Dave Filoni|{{WebCite|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2012/03/21/star-wars-the-clone-wars-looking-back-at-season-4|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars - Looking Back at Season 4|author=Goldman, Eric|date=2012-03-21|format=Online interview|archivedate=20160324155428}}}} [[File:JarJarBinksConceptArt-AoEpI.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Concept art of Jar Jar Binks]] The Gungans first appeared in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]]. The name "Gungan" came, according to George Lucas in an interview, from his son [[Jett Lucas|Jett's]] name for tractors and trucks.{{WebCite|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-news/jar-jar-binks-a-digital-star-is-born-50301|text=Jar Jar Binks: A Digital Star Is Born|author=Dunn, Jancee|date=1999-06-24|work=Rolling Stone|archivedate=20200509122715}} In the real world, the word "Gungan" can also refer to any member of an Australian genus of frogs, [[Wikipedia:Uperoleia|''Uperoleia'']].{{WebCite|url=http://www.turtlecare.com.au/difference-between-cane-toads-and-native-australian-frogs.php|text=How to tell the difference between cane toads and native Australian frogs|work=turtlecare|archivedate=20111004080456}} Originally, the Gungans were meant to be wiped out along with Otoh Gunga prior to the Battle of Naboo, and therefore, they didn't participate in the battle, as seen in early storyboards of the film. As genocide was judged to be too dark for the film, thus, the story was adjusted.''[[Star Wars Storyboards: The Prequel Trilogy]]'' By allying with the Naboo and doing so in the ancient Sacred Place, which is located in a forest, the Gungans helped support the "symbiotic relationship" metaphor that{{InsiderCite|216|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the Star Wars Galaxy|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the ''Star Wars'' Galaxy}} director [[George Lucas]] conceived of for the [[prequel trilogy]]. Tying into how the Force has a [[Cosmic Force|cosmic]] half and [[Living Force|living]] half, which feed into each other,[[The High Republic Adventures (2021) 7|''The High Republic Adventures'' (2021) 7]] nature is said to be at its best when it is used for the mutual benefit of all living beings.
